title: Runyard: a Mac app for keeping and running code samples
description: Runyard is a Mac app for keeping and running code samples. Pick a template and get a playground with an editor, live preview and terminal. AI coding agents can create and run playgrounds from the command line.
h1:
Pick a template.
It runs in a second.
lead: Runyard is a Mac app for keeping and running code samples. Pick a template and get a playground with an editor, live preview and terminal. AI coding agents can create and run playgrounds from the command line.
featuresTitle: A home for your code samples
featuresLead: Try a library, check a claim, build a demo. Start from a template, and find it again in the library next month.

features.alt: Runyard's template picker listing eight templates, with React 19 + Vite selected
features.title: Pick a template, running in a second
features.body: Eight built-in templates: HTML, React 19, React 18, Vue 3, Node + TypeScript, Python, Go and Hono. They run on the toolchains already on your Mac.

features.alt: Runyard's web playground workspace: code on the left, live preview on the right, output below
features.title: Edit code, see the result
features.body: A Monaco editor that feels like VS Code. Pages refresh as you type, services keep running, and the terminal is right below.

features.alt: Runyard's library, with running playgrounds listed first
features.title: A library you can find things in
features.body: Every playground is a plain folder in ~/Runyard. Running ones come first. Add notes, turn on auto-clean, move the rest to the Trash.

features.alt: Runyard's service workspace: a request panel on the right showing 200 OK and the response
features.title: A request panel for services
features.body: When a service such as Hono is running, send requests and read responses right next to the code. No extra tool.

agentsTitle: A command line for AI agents
agentsLead: Coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex create and run a playground with one command. You see what they made, and what is still running, in the library.
termComment: # teach your agent to use runyard (once)
termNote: The command line comes with the app: add it to PATH in Settings; it is always available in the built-in terminal.

points.title: Create and run in one command
points.body: new --run --json returns the path, the URL and where the logs are. Errors carry a code and the next command to run.

points.title: Install the skill once
points.body: Run runyard skill install, or click Install in Settings, and Claude Code and Codex know how to use it.

points.title: See what agents did
points.body: Playgrounds made by an agent carry a badge in the library, name the agent, and can be filtered by creator.

agentShotAlt: A playground an agent just made: a library row with a Claude Code badge, and a notice that it was created and run
downloadLead: Free and open source. All you need is a Mac.
unsignedLead: This build is not notarised by Apple yet, so macOS blocks it the first time you open it. Right-click → Open on older systems; on newer ones do the steps below once, and it opens normally from then on.
unsignedSteps: Open the .dmg and drag Runyard to Applications first, then open it from Applications (opening it inside the .dmg causes problems)
Double-click Runyard. When macOS says it cannot verify the developer, click Done
Open System Settings → Privacy & Security, click Open Anyway under Security, then enter your login password
olderMac: macOS 14 and earlier: right-click Runyard in Applications and choose Open.
terminalLead: If you like the command line, do it in one step:
toolchain: Playgrounds run on the Node, Python and Go already on your Mac. If something is missing, the app tells you how to install it.
footerTagline: The Mac app for keeping and running code samples
network: Network: once a day the app asks GitHub whether a new version exists, with no identifiers.
